transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-16T10:00:00-07:00
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lisa Park (NexaHead ML), Jamal Ortiz (Nexa Platform), Priya Menon (Nexa Security), Evan Cho (Data Eng)

Summary: Quick check-in on onboarding and environment readiness; confirm service account/VPC details and schedule perf run.

[00:00] Avery: okay good morning everyone, um we'll do a quick 30ish minute sync i see we have 42 minutes on the calendar but should be fine. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account.
[00:18] Lisa: thanks Avery, mornings, quick note Jamal's got the network bits half done so maybe we can unblock the perf run today.
[00:29] Jamal: yeah sorry morning, we've got the subnet reserved, still need to create the service account and the VPC peering request, will do that by end of day.
[00:42] Samir: great, Samir from the SE side, I'll own the perf script and the config for the dedicated run, and we'll also run a hosted baseline so you can see delta in latency and cost.
[01:10] Priya: hi, Priya on security, quick flag — we need KMS controls, key rotation policy, and confirmation about where audit logs will be stored. Are you using an HSM option?
[01:30] Avery: yep good question, we do support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; i will share the architecture note and the SOC2 pack after the call.
[01:50] Lisa: perfect. On timelines: we want to have initial perf numbers by next week, ideally before our steering committee on Thursday.
[02:12] Samir: understood, we'll target an initial perf run tomorrow once jamal shares service account & peering; the test is ~1 hour and will produce per-route p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
[02:45] Evan: quick question — any special tokenizer or input preprocessing we need to provide? our pipeline uses sentencepiece and some custom pre-token normalizer.
[03:05] Samir: fine, we can accept raw text but share the pre-token steps; we did see some tokenization mismatches before — the runtime expects byte-level bpe for the open model variant, i'll note that in the test plan.
[03:27] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[04:00] Jamal: about the VPC, we prefer VPC peering over public endpoints, is that fully supported for dedicated? we've read some docs but want to confirm.
[04:20] Avery: yes VPC peering supported for Dedicated and Private modes; hosted API uses TLS public endpoints but we can do private link or peering for enterprise. i'll include the peering runbook link.
[04:45] Priya: regarding data residency, some of our PHI-related logs must stay in region eu-west-1; is that a problem?
[05:05] Samir: we have region pinning and you can pin model execution to specific regions, but for log retention we need to check the retention policies; i'll include specifics but initial answer is yes we can keep things in eu-west-1 with Private.
[05:40] Lisa: okay nice, also what about RBAC and SSO — our SREs will want SAML SSO and per-role permissions so platform teams can't access ML dev logs.
[06:05] Avery: Redwood supports SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC; we'll send the SSO integration doc and a sample role mapping.
[06:30] Jamal: workflow for infra access — i'll create service account, provide the PEM and the role we need?
[06:45] Avery: for the test we just need a service account with network peering permissions and the ability to mount the bucket for sample data; we prefer a scoped role, we'll document the minimum required IAM perms.
[07:10] Priya: on encryption — do you allow customer KMS keys or only Redwood-managed?
[07:25] Samir: both, you can bring your own key (BYOK) via KMS integration; we also offer HSM-backed keys for tighter compliance. we'll note the latency/cost tradeoffs for HSM.
[07:50] Lisa: excellent. Can we also ask about model variants — we want to try a quantized 8-bit variant to reduce cost but worried about quality regression.
[08:10] Samir: yes we recommend starting with 8-bit quantized for throughput tests; we monitor quality with an eval set and we can run A/B to compare token-level deltas. our Optimize team provides suggested quantization profiles based on your workload.
[08:42] Evan: do you store prefixes or KV cache? our workload is chat-like and we'd like to reuse prefixes across calls.
[09:00] Samir: yes we support prefix and KV caching — note that's sometimes transcribed in docs as 'K V cache' — we'll include caching config in the perf plan; caching reduces per-token costs significantly for chat workloads.
[09:25] Lisa: any concerns about latency p99 with caching enabled?
[09:40] Samir: caching improves p50/p95 but p99 can still be affected by cold starts and IO; we'll run through steady-state tests and cold start tests.
[10:05] Avery: ok, so immediate blockers — jamal needs to share service account + peering, priya needs to confirm KMS policy details. everyone aligned?
[10:22] Jamal: yes i'll send peering ticket and the service account details by EOD.
[10:30] Priya: i'll confirm key rotation policy and whether HSM required for PHI workloads by Monday.
[10:40] Samir: i'll post the perf run script to the shared drive and ping when it's ready, plan is to run hosted baseline then dedicated run and capture cost numbers.
[11:05] Lisa: sounds good, please also provide the token-level cost breakdown so we can plug into our TCO models.
[11:20] Avery: yeah we'll include token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 numbers, and a short summary slide deck.
[11:40] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[12:00] Avery: any other questions?
[12:12] Lisa: one last item — legal asked if you have a standard DPA and addendum for PHI, can you share that with procurement?
[12:30] Avery: yes we have a DPA and a PHI addendum template, i'll put those in the security pack link.
[12:50] Jamal: one small nit — will the perf run require sample data in S3 or can we stream? we prefer S3 object access.
[13:10] Samir: S3 access is fine; we'll request read-only access to the test bucket or you can rsync the sample dataset to our test runner inside the VPC.
[13:35] Evan: estimating expected throughput — we plan to hit ~200 QPS in steady state for our peak tests, just so you know.
[13:55] Samir: noted, 200 QPS is reasonable for the dedicated pool test, we'll size batch sizes accordingly and measure latency.
[14:20] Lisa: anything else from Redwood?
[14:30] Avery: i think that's it. we'll send the security pack, run the perf, and reconvene next week.
[14:45] Priya: thanks all.
[15:00] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: autogenerated, some speaker labels approximate. There are a few inaudible sections. References/shared links: sec pack (https://redwood.app/secure/nexahealth/sec-pack), perf spreadsheet (will be shared after run).
